scenes.line1: Why use AsNoTracking in EF Core?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why AsNoTracking is a big deal in Entity Framework Core? Is it just a performance trick, or does it change more?

scenes.label: Tracking
scenes.sub: EF Core watches entities for changes to save updates.
scenes.say: With change tracking, Entity Framework Core keeps an eye on your entities. It knows what you change and can save those updates back to the database.

scenes.label: NoTracking
scenes.sub: Entities are read-only and updates aren't tracked.
scenes.say: AsNoTracking flips the switch. Now, entities are just snapshots. No updates are tracked, so you can't save changes later.
Tracking uses more memory and CPU, since it monitors every entity. AsNoTracking skips all that, making read-heavy queries much faster.
Here's how I make a query read-only. I add AsNoTracking to the users query, making it faster when I don't need to update anything.

scenes.question: Can you update entities from AsNoTracking?
scenes.right: No—you must reattach or track them first.
scenes.say: Watch out: you can't update entities fetched with AsNoTracking unless you reattach or start tracking them again. SaveChanges won't work on them directly.
